task.instruction: Advise the service director whether to change the failed-delivery workflow before the autumn peak. Give a concrete next move and answer the concern that another study will waste the remaining preparation window.
deliverables: the evidence driving the timing decision
a dated review or reversal trigger
hardConstraints: Use only claims supported by the supplied documents and prior records.
Cite the decision evidence with [doc-02] and [doc-04].
The escalation line must remain available and any operational change must be reversible within 48 hours.
Separate observed facts, interpretation, and recommendation.

documents.title: Peak readiness calendar
documents.content: Uniform orders close on 18 August. The staff photography session is 21 August. Neither date changes the delivery workflow.

documents.title: Two-week callback trial
documents.content: For 420 failed deliveries, a callback within 20 minutes reduced repeat contacts from 31% to 19%. Rural routes were 8% of the trial but represent 27% of peak failures.

documents.title: Autumn change capacity
documents.content: The team can train one workflow before 1 September. Waiting beyond 12 August leaves no rehearsal week. The current process can continue without contractual penalty.

documents.title: Rural escalation review
documents.content: Three rural callbacks reached drivers after coverage ended. The existing escalation line resolved all three; removing it would have prolonged the failures.

documents.title: Dispatcher feedback
documents.content: Dispatchers support faster callbacks but say two simultaneous scripts would increase handoff mistakes. They prefer either a short rural test or one monitored workflow.

target_a.content:
Situation: A museum must choose a new ticketing layout before the holiday season.
Shared facts [history-01-01-fact]: The A/B test covers weekdays only; the vendor needs a production choice in nine days; either layout can be rolled back overnight.
Decision: Extend the test through one weekend and reserve the reversible deployment slot.
Reasoning: Both choices preserve a correction path, but they price the missing weekend signal differently.

Situation: A field team is selecting one of two soil sensors for a six-month study.
Shared facts [history-01-02-fact]: Sensor K is more precise in the lab; Sensor M has three years of field maintenance records; the planting window closes in twelve days.
Message excerpt: Run both sensors side by side for four days at the field site before ordering the full set.

Situation: A volunteer network is deciding whether to open a second evening shift.
Shared facts [history-01-03-fact]: Demand estimates vary by 35%; trained coverage is confirmed for six weeks; waiting another month loses the donated venue.
Retrospective: Use two pop-up evenings to measure arrivals before committing the recurring roster.

Situation: A design team must choose whether to translate a guide before usability findings arrive.
Shared facts [history-01-04-fact]: Translation takes three weeks; the launch is in four weeks; prior products show mixed demand across the two target regions.
log.decision=Translate the critical onboarding pages first and wait for the moderated sessions before expanding.

Situation: A laboratory freezer alarm has one unexplained late notification.
Shared facts [history-01-05-fact]: The delay cannot be reproduced; a firmware patch is available; the patch changes an untested failover path.
Decision: Reproduce the failover path in a spare unit before installing the patch.

Situation: A childcare center discovers that both proposed playground surfaces exceed the legal lead limit.
Shared facts [history-01-06-fact]: The inspection is confirmed by two accredited tests and children cannot use the area until remediation.
Message excerpt: Reject both surfaces and begin remediation under the statutory protocol.

Situation: A public grant deadline arrives while one applicant's ownership disclosure is missing.
Shared facts [history-01-07-fact]: The disclosure is mandatory and cannot be cured after award; funds can be reallocated next quarter.
Retrospective: Exclude the incomplete application and preserve the documented reallocation route.

Situation: A restaurant is choosing a seasonal supplier after its regular supplier loses capacity.
Shared facts [history-01-08-fact]: Supplier A can cover 70% immediately with known quality; Supplier B can cover all volume but has one incomplete audit; menu printing starts tomorrow.
log.decision=Split the first order, complete Supplier B's audit, and retain an editable menu insert.
